I found the cause. In the desktop app, clicking any "Open the pull request" link does nothing. In a browser the links work.

**Why it happens**

1. All the "Open the pull request" links are ordinary `target="_blank"` links to GitHub:
   - `server/views/projects/_branch.eta:87`
   - `server/views/projects/_pushed.eta:3`
   - `server/views/_folder.eta:25-26`
2. In the desktop app, `server/public/desktop.js:21-30` catches the click on every `a[target="_blank"]` and cancels it with `preventDefault()`. `run()` (`desktop.js:43-45`) then passes the address to `desktop.openInBrowser(url)`.
3. The shell's `open_in_browser` command (`tauri/src-tauri/src/main.rs:318-326`) only opens addresses that pass `may_open_in_browser` (`main.rs:265-269`). That check only allows the server's own origin and `preview.localhost`. A test asserts this: `https://example.com` is refused (`main.rs:469`).
4. A GitHub address is refused, so the command returns an error. `desktop.js:29` only writes that error to the console. The link's own navigation was already cancelled, so nothing opens and nothing is shown.

The "Needs you" items that point somewhere else (`home/_needs-you.eta:19`, `projects/_work.eta:29`) go through the same path and are blocked the same way. "Open the app" links still work, because they're on the server's own origin (`/f/<id>/host/open`, `server/main.js:750`).

The restriction itself makes sense: a page shouldn't be able to make the shell open any address it likes, such as `file:` paths or other schemes. But it was written for "Open in browser", and `desktop.js` uses it for every outside link.

**What I'd change**

- **`tauri/src-tauri/src/main.rs`:** have `open_in_browser`, or a separate `open_external` command, also accept any `https://` address. Keep refusing other schemes. Update the test at `main.rs:463-470`: `https://github.com/...` should pass, while `file:` and `http://` to other hosts still fail.
- **`server/public/desktop.js`:** if the shell refuses an address, fall back to `window.open(url, '_blank')` instead of failing silently. That way a refused link still does something visible.
- To be stricter than "any https", the server could tell the shell the project's remote host (e.g. `github.com`). That's probably more than this needs.

The shell is Rust, so it needs rebuilding (`dist-shell`) before you'll see the fix in the desktop app.

I've made the fix, but I couldn't build or run anything, so it hasn't been tested yet.

**What changed**
- **The desktop app's link check** (`tauri/src-tauri/src/main.rs`): before, the app only opened its own pages and preview pages in your browser, so it refused GitHub and the click did nothing. Now it also opens any `https` address, so "Open the pull request" opens GitHub in your system browser. Plain `http` links still only open for the app's own server and its preview. Other address types, like `file:` links or Windows settings pages, are still refused. I updated the existing test to match (`the_browser_opens_this_server_its_preview_and_https_only`).
- **A fallback in the page** (`server/public/desktop.js`): if the app still refuses an address, for example a pull request on a self-hosted Git server over plain `http`, the link now opens the way an ordinary link would instead of doing nothing.

This also fixes other links that point outside Prelude and failed the same way, such as the "Needs you" items. No designs changed, because the pages look and behave as designed.

**To check it**
1. Run `cargo test` in `tauri/src-tauri`, and `npm test`.
2. Rebuild the desktop app. The fix is in its Rust code, so you won't see a difference until it's rebuilt.
3. Push a branch, then click "Open the pull request" on its row and in the "Pushed …" notice. GitHub should open in your browser.
4. Make sure "Open in browser" and Pop out still work as before.

The full write-up is in `prelude/fixes/the-open-the-pull-request-links-don-t-seem-to-work-at/NOTES.md`.

There's a script to build the desktop app, but none to run it. From `package.json`:

- **`npm run build:shell`** does a release build of the app and copies it to `dist-shell/Prelude.exe`.
- **`npm run test:shell`** runs the app's Rust tests (`cargo test`). These are the tests I updated.

To run the app, start `dist-shell\Prelude.exe` directly. It uses a Prelude that's already running on port 4200 (from `npm start`), or starts one itself if none is.

To try this fix:
1. Run `npm run test:shell`, then `npm run build:shell`.
2. If a Prelude server is already running from `npm start`, restart it so it serves the new `desktop.js`. If the desktop app starts its own server, that will already have the new file.
3. Launch `dist-shell\Prelude.exe` and click "Open the pull request".

The build needs the desktop app to be closed, because Windows won't let it overwrite `Prelude.exe` while it's running.
